Maria C.: Hey team — data-sync job needs read access to the prod logs bucket for analytics exports. What is the least-priv we should give? I was going to add Storage Object Viewer at the analytics project but that feels broad.
Alejandro R.: don't grant project-level if it's only that bucket. give bucket-level role to the service account, and ideally via a group so you can rotate membership easily.
Emily (sec): Agree with Alejandro. bucket-level binding + IAM Condition to limit by prefix + restrict to the serviceAccount is the right approach. Also double-check whether exported logs include PII; if so we need a redaction/export review. Which SA are you using?
Maria C.: The SA is analytics-sync@analytics-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com. Job runs from the analytics project (cross-project read). It is kicked off by Cloud Build cron. Can we avoid keys?
Josh P.: yes — avoid long-lived keys. Use Workload Identity or service account impersonation. For Cloud Build, you can let Cloud Build impersonate the SA (short-lived tokens). For GKE use Workload Identity.
Alejandro R.: Example command to add bucket-level viewer:
```bash
gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding gs://prod-logs \
  --member='serviceAccount:analytics-sync@analytics-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com' \
  --role='roles/storage.objectViewer'
```
Add a group instead of the SA directly if you prefer: `group:analytics-syncers@redwood.com`.
Emily (sec): If logs have sensitive fields, add an IAM Condition to the binding so it only applies to the object name prefix you need. Example condition (GCP IAM condition expression):
```
condition: expr = "resource.name.startsWith('projects/_/buckets/prod-logs/objects/analytics_exports/') && request.auth.claims.email == 'analytics-sync@analytics-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com'"
title: "restrict-to-exports-prefix-and-sa"
```
That limits risk if another object path exists. Also: enable Data Access audit logs for the bucket and tag the ticket for compliance review if you expect PII.
Maria C.: Got it. I’ll create the `analytics-syncers@redwood.com` group and PR the bucket-level binding with the condition. Quick follow-up: do we need read access to bucket lifecycle or IAM? No — just object read.
Emily (sec): Correct — do NOT grant `roles/storage.admin` or project-level viewer. Only `roles/storage.objectViewer` at the bucket (with condition). File a compliance ticket if you need to export/redact logs. :thumbsup:
Alejandro R.: One more note: if the job runs from a different project, make sure the member string uses the full serviceAccount principal. Also consider rotating the service account by replacing group membership when needed.
Maria C.: thanks all — I’ll open the PR and link the infra ticket. ping me if you spot anything missing.
infra-bot: Ticket #INC-23456 created by Maria C. (analytics-sync bucket perms) — https://infra.redwood.dev/tickets/INC-23456
Maria C.: ack, adding the compliance label and linking the doc https://intranet.redwood.dev/security/iam-guidelines.
Emily (sec): LGTM once PR has the condition expression and audit log checklist.
Josh P.: :rocket:
